1.title: ITIL with DevOps and PRINCE2
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: eye til with dev ops and prince two. It covers the exam area eye til and other frameworks. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Understand how eye til collaborates with dev ops practices and how the two are complementary in the product and service development lifecycle. Understand why project management is important in eye til and how eye til and prince two are complementary. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: eye til and other frameworks (two point five percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: ITIL and DevOps
1.text: eye til and dev ops. dev ops is a culture and set of practices that joins development and operations to deliver software faster and more reliably, with collaboration, automation, continuous integration and delivery, and fast feedback. Shared aims. Both aim at value, collaboration, feedback and improvement. dev ops brings. Fast delivery, automation, continuous integration and delivery, a culture of shared ownership. eye til brings. Governance, a whole-lifecycle view, service quality and support, practices such as incident, problem and change. Together. Teams move fast and stay in control; operate and support feed learning back into discover, design and build.

1.title: ITIL and DevOps, continued
1.text: eye til and dev ops. The figure shows this: dev ops and eye til cover different strengths across the lifecycle activities. Exam tip: Complementary, not competing. dev ops adds speed and automation; eye til adds governance and the full lifecycle view.

1.title: ITIL and PRINCE2
1.text: eye til and prince two. prince two is a project management method. Many changes and new products are delivered as projects, so project management matters inside eye til. eye til gives. The lifecycle, practices, value focus for running products and services. prince two gives. A structured way to plan, control and deliver a project (business case, stages, controls, roles). Together. Projects deliver the new or changed product; eye til operates and improves it afterwards.

1.title: ITIL and PRINCE2, continued
1.text: eye til and prince two. Why project management matters in eye til: it provides planning, resources, risk and progress control when building or changing products and services, and hands over to operate, deliver and support. Exam tip: prince two equals projects. eye til equals the life of products and services. Complementary. Exam tip: Only one mark covers other frameworks. The safe answer is almost always complementary: dev ops adds speed and automation, prince two adds project control, eye til adds the lifecycle and governance.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which statement best describes the relationship between eye til and dev ops? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: They are complementary: dev ops adds speed and automation, eye til adds governance and a lifecycle view. The two complement each other.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company uses prince two to deliver a new customer app, then runs it using eye til practices. What does this show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: eye til and prince two are complementary. Projects deliver; eye til operates and improves.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) prince two is a project management method. (two) dev ops emphasizes collaboration and automation. (three) eye til cannot be used with agile teams. (four) prince two is a replacement for the eye til value chain. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: one and two. Those two statements are correct.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). eye til and dev ops are blank in the product and service development lifecycle. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Complementary. They complement each other.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Why is project management important in eye til? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It provides planning and control when building or changing products and services. Projects deliver changes in a controlled way.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which dev ops practice supports faster releases? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Continuous integration and delivery. Continuous integration and delivery speed up releases.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does dev ops combine? Answer: Development and operations, with collaboration and automation. Question two. What is prince two? Answer: A project management method. Question three. Are eye til and dev ops competing or complementary? Answer: Complementary.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does eye til add to a dev ops team? Answer: Governance, a whole-lifecycle view and service quality and support practices. Question five. Why does eye til value project management? Answer: Projects deliver new or changed products and services in a planned, controlled way. Question six. What happens after a project delivers a product? Answer: It is operated, delivered and supported, and improved, using eye til.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. dev ops: development plus operations; speed and automation. prince two: project management method. With eye til: complementary, not competing. eye til adds: governance, lifecycle view, practices.
